passages.text: These are the names of the sons of Israel who went to Egypt with Jacob, each with his family: Reuben, Simeon, Levi, and Judah; Issachar, Zebulun, and Benjamin; Dan and Naphtali; Gad and Asher.
passages.sermon:
Jacob was the father of the sons of Israel.
Jacob went to Egypt.
The sons of Israel went with Jacob.
Each son brought his family.
These are the names of the sons of Israel who went to Egypt:
Reuben went to Egypt.
Simeon went to Egypt.
Levi went to Egypt.
Judah went to Egypt.
Issachar went to Egypt.
Zebulun went to Egypt.
Benjamin went to Egypt.
Dan went to Egypt.
Naphtali went to Egypt.
Gad went to Egypt.
Asher went to Egypt.
passages.original: וְאֵ֗לֶּה שְׁמוֹת֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל הַבָּאִ֖ים מִצְרָ֑יְמָה אֵ֣ת יַעֲקֹ֔ב אִ֥ישׁ וּבֵית֖וֹ בָּֽאוּ׃ רְאוּבֵ֣ן שִׁמְע֔וֹן לֵוִ֖י וִיהוּדָֽה׃ יִשָּׂשכָ֥ר זְבוּלֻ֖ן וּבְנְיָמִֽן׃ דָּ֥ן וְנַפְתָּלִ֖י גָּ֥ד וְאָשֵֽׁר׃

passages.text: The descendants of Jacob numbered seventy in all, including Joseph, who was already in Egypt.
passages.sermon:
Jacob was the father of a large family.
Jacob had many descendants.
The total number of Jacob’s descendants was seventy.
Joseph was one of Jacob’s sons.
Joseph was already living in Egypt.
passages.original: וַֽיְהִ֗י כָּל־ נֶ֛פֶשׁ יֹצְאֵ֥י יֶֽרֶךְ־ יַעֲקֹ֖ב שִׁבְעִ֣ים נָ֑פֶשׁ וְיוֹסֵ֖ף הָיָ֥ה בְמִצְרָֽיִם׃

passages.text: Now Joseph and all his brothers and all that generation died, but the Israelites were fruitful and increased rapidly; they multiplied and became exceedingly numerous, so that the land was filled with them.
passages.sermon:
Joseph died.
All his brothers died.
Everyone from that generation died.
The Israelites lived in Egypt.
The Israelites had many children.
The Israelites increased in number.
The Israelites became very strong.
The Israelites became extremely numerous.
The land became filled with the Israelites.
passages.original: וַיָּ֤מָת יוֹסֵף֙ וְכָל־ אֶחָ֔יו וְכֹ֖ל הַדּ֥וֹר הַהֽוּא׃ וּבְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל פָּר֧וּ וַֽיִּשְׁרְצ֛וּ וַיִּרְבּ֥וּ וַיַּֽעַצְמ֖וּ בִּמְאֹ֣ד מְאֹ֑ד וַתִּמָּלֵ֥א הָאָ֖רֶץ אֹתָֽם׃פ

passages.text: Then a new king, who did not know Joseph, came to power in Egypt.
passages.sermon: A new king began to rule in Egypt.\r\nThis king did not know Joseph.
passages.original: וַיָּ֥קָם מֶֽלֶךְ־ חָדָ֖שׁ עַל־ מִצְרָ֑יִם אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹֽא־ יָדַ֖ע אֶת־ יוֹסֵֽף׃

passages.text: “Look,” he said to his people, “the Israelites have become too numerous and too powerful for us.
passages.sermon:
A new king ruled Egypt.
This king did not know Joseph.
The king spoke to his people.
He said, “Look at the Israelites.
The Israelites are a large group.
The Israelites are strong.
The Israelites are more numerous and powerful than we are.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֖אמֶר אֶל־ עַמּ֑וֹ הִנֵּ֗ה עַ֚ם בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל רַ֥ב וְעָצ֖וּם מִמֶּֽנּוּ׃

passages.text: Come, let us deal shrewdly with them, or they will increase even more; and if a war breaks out, they may join our enemies, fight against us, and leave the country.”
passages.sermon:
A new king ruled Egypt.
This king did not know Joseph.
He spoke to his people.
He said, “Let us act wisely toward the Israelites.
If we do not, they will become even more numerous.
If war happens, they may join our enemies.
They may fight against us.
They may leave the land.”
passages.original: הָ֥בָה נִֽתְחַכְּמָ֖ה ל֑וֹ פֶּן־ יִרְבֶּ֗ה וְהָיָ֞ה כִּֽי־ תִקְרֶ֤אנָה מִלְחָמָה֙ וְנוֹסַ֤ף גַּם־ הוּא֙ עַל־ שֹׂ֣נְאֵ֔ינוּ וְנִלְחַם־ בָּ֖נוּ וְעָלָ֥ה מִן־ הָאָֽרֶץ׃

passages.text: So the Egyptians appointed taskmasters over the Israelites to oppress them with forced labor. As a result, they built Pithom and Rameses as store cities for Pharaoh.
passages.sermon:
The Egyptians ruled over the Israelites.
The Egyptians appointed taskmasters over the Israelites.
The Egyptians wanted to oppress the Israelites.
The Egyptians forced the Israelites to work hard.
The Israelites built cities for Pharaoh.
The Israelites built Pithom for Pharaoh.
The Israelites built Rameses for Pharaoh.
These cities stored supplies for Pharaoh.
passages.original: וַיָּשִׂ֤ימוּ עָלָיו֙ שָׂרֵ֣י מִסִּ֔ים לְמַ֥עַן עַנֹּת֖וֹ בְּסִבְלֹתָ֑ם וַיִּ֜בֶן עָרֵ֤י מִסְכְּנוֹת֙ לְפַרְעֹ֔ה אֶת־ פִּתֹ֖ם וְאֶת־ רַעַמְסֵֽס׃

passages.text: But the more they were oppressed, the more they multiplied and flourished; so the Egyptians came to dread the Israelites.
passages.sermon:
The Egyptians oppressed the Israelites.
They made their lives hard.
But the Israelites grew in number.
They became stronger and flourished.
The Egyptians began to fear the Israelites.
passages.original: וְכַאֲשֶׁר֙ יְעַנּ֣וּ אֹת֔וֹ כֵּ֥ן יִרְבֶּ֖ה וְכֵ֣ן יִפְרֹ֑ץ וַיָּקֻ֕צוּ מִפְּנֵ֖י בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: They worked the Israelites ruthlessly and made their lives bitter with hard labor in brick and mortar, and with all kinds of work in the fields. Every service they imposed was harsh.
passages.sermon:
The Egyptians forced the Israelites to work very hard.
The Egyptians treated the Israelites with cruelty.
The Egyptians made the lives of the Israelites bitter.
They gave the Israelites hard labor.
They made the Israelites work with brick and mortar.
They made the Israelites do all kinds of work in the fields.
Every job the Egyptians gave the Israelites was harsh.
The Egyptians made the Israelites suffer with cruel service.
passages.original: וַיַּעֲבִ֧דוּ מִצְרַ֛יִם אֶת־ בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בְּפָֽרֶךְ׃ וַיְמָרְר֨וּ אֶת־ חַיֵּיהֶ֜ם בַּעֲבֹדָ֣ה קָשָׁ֗ה בְּחֹ֙מֶר֙ וּבִלְבֵנִ֔ים וּבְכָל־ עֲבֹדָ֖ה בַּשָּׂדֶ֑ה אֵ֚ת כָּל־ עֲבֹ֣דָתָ֔ם אֲשֶׁר־ עָבְד֥וּ בָהֶ֖ם בְּפָֽרֶךְ׃

passages.text: Then the king of Egypt said to the Hebrew midwives, whose names were Shiphrah and Puah, “When you help the Hebrew women give birth, observe them on the birthstools. If the child is a son, kill him; but if it is a daughter, let her live.”
passages.sermon:
The king of Egypt spoke to the Hebrew midwives.
The name of one midwife was Shiphrah.
The name of the other midwife was Puah.
The king gave them instructions.
He said, “When you help the Hebrew women give birth, watch them on the birthstools.
If the baby is a son, kill him.
If the baby is a daughter, let her live.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ מִצְרַ֔יִם לַֽמְיַלְּדֹ֖ת הָֽעִבְרִיֹּ֑ת אֲשֶׁ֨ר שֵׁ֤ם הָֽאַחַת֙ שִׁפְרָ֔ה וְשֵׁ֥ם הַשֵּׁנִ֖ית פּוּעָֽה׃ וַיֹּ֗אמֶר בְּיַלֶּדְכֶן֙ אֶת־ הָֽעִבְרִיּ֔וֹת וּרְאִיתֶ֖ן עַל־ הָאָבְנָ֑יִם אִם־ בֵּ֥ן הוּא֙ וַהֲמִתֶּ֣ן אֹת֔וֹ וְאִם־ בַּ֥ת הִ֖יא וָחָֽיָה׃

passages.text: The midwives, however, feared God and did not do as the king of Egypt had instructed; they let the boys live.
passages.sermon:
The midwives feared God.
They did not obey the king of Egypt.
The king of Egypt told them to kill the Hebrew baby boys.
The midwives let the boys live.
passages.original: וַתִּירֶ֤אןָ הַֽמְיַלְּדֹת֙ אֶת־ הָ֣אֱלֹהִ֔ים וְלֹ֣א עָשׂ֔וּ כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר דִּבֶּ֥ר אֲלֵיהֶ֖ן מֶ֣לֶךְ מִצְרָ֑יִם וַתְּחַיֶּ֖יןָ אֶת־ הַיְלָדִֽים׃

passages.text: So the king of Egypt summoned the midwives and asked them, “Why have you done this? Why have you let the boys live?”
passages.sermon:
The king of Egypt ruled over the land.
\r\nHe had great power.
\r\nHe called for the Hebrew midwives.
\r\nHe spoke to them directly.
\r\nHe asked them a question.
\r\nHe said, “Why did you do this?”
\r\nHe wanted to know their reason.
\r\nHe said, “Why did you let the boys live?”
\r\nHe noticed they did not kill the baby boys.
\r\nHe wanted an explanation.
passages.original: וַיִּקְרָ֤א מֶֽלֶךְ־ מִצְרַ֙יִם֙ לַֽמְיַלְּדֹ֔ת וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לָהֶ֔ן מַדּ֥וּעַ עֲשִׂיתֶ֖ן הַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֑ה וַתְּחַיֶּ֖יןָ אֶת־ הַיְלָדִֽים׃

passages.text: The midwives answered Pharaoh, “The Hebrew women are not like the Egyptian women, for they are vigorous and give birth before a midwife arrives.”
passages.sermon:
The midwives spoke to Pharaoh.
They said, “The Hebrew women are not like the Egyptian women.
The Hebrew women are strong.
They give birth quickly.
They give birth before the midwife arrives.”
passages.original: וַתֹּאמַ֤רְןָ הַֽמְיַלְּדֹת֙ אֶל־ פַּרְעֹ֔ה כִּ֣י לֹ֧א כַנָּשִׁ֛ים הַמִּצְרִיֹּ֖ת הָֽעִבְרִיֹּ֑ת כִּֽי־ חָי֣וֹת הֵ֔נָּה בְּטֶ֨רֶם תָּב֧וֹא אֲלֵהֶ֛ן הַמְיַלֶּ֖דֶת וְיָלָֽדוּ׃

passages.text: So God was good to the midwives, and the people multiplied and became even more numerous.
passages.sermon: God showed kindness to the midwives.\r\nThe people of Israel grew in number.\r\nThe people became very strong.
passages.original: וַיֵּ֥יטֶב אֱלֹהִ֖ים לַֽמְיַלְּדֹ֑ת וַיִּ֧רֶב הָעָ֛ם וַיַּֽעַצְמ֖וּ מְאֹֽד׃

passages.text: And because the midwives feared God, He gave them families of their own.
passages.sermon: The midwives feared God.\r\nGod saw that the midwives feared Him.\r\nGod gave the midwives families of their own.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֕י כִּֽי־ יָֽרְא֥וּ הַֽמְיַלְּדֹ֖ת אֶת־ הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים וַיַּ֥עַשׂ לָהֶ֖ם בָּתִּֽים׃

passages.text: Then Pharaoh commanded all his people: “Every son born to the Hebrews you must throw into the Nile, but every daughter you may allow to live.”
passages.sermon:
Pharaoh was the king of Egypt.
Pharaoh gave an order to all his people.
Pharaoh said, “You must throw every Hebrew son who is born into the Nile River.
You must let every Hebrew daughter live.”
passages.original: וַיְצַ֣ו פַּרְעֹ֔ה לְכָל־ עַמּ֖וֹ לֵאמֹ֑ר כָּל־ הַבֵּ֣ן הַיִּלּ֗וֹד הַיְאֹ֙רָה֙ תַּשְׁלִיכֻ֔הוּ וְכָל־ הַבַּ֖ת תְּחַיּֽוּן׃ס
